title: Chrome for Realtors on Mac: Voice Help for MLS, CRM and Paperwork Tabs
metaTitle: Chrome for Realtors on Mac: Tabs, Logins and Paperwork
description: Chrome for realtors on Mac: tab groups, pinned tabs, @tabs search and shortcuts for MLS, CRM and paperwork, plus voice help from Lazur.
secondaryKeywords: Chrome tab groups for real estate
intro: Chrome for realtors on Mac is the standard Google Chrome app, set up for the work you do all day: MLS and CRM logins, listing copy and document chasing. The fastest setup uses tab groups for each deal, pinned tabs for daily portals, and @tabs to find any open page. Lazur adds voice help in the same window.
tldr: Chrome for realtors on Mac is regular Chrome. The gain comes from setup: tab groups, pinned tabs, a separate profile and @tabs search.
Chrome 151 and later need macOS 13 or later. Check your version under Chrome > About Google Chrome.
Transaction paperwork and chasing documents are the loudest complaints in public agent comments. Build your browser around them.
Lazur sees the screen only while you hold ⌥ ⌘. It points, guides one click at a time and does not click for you.

blocks.text: No survey I could find breaks out which browser agents use. So treat this page as a workflow guide, not a usage report. The Chrome features below come from Google's own tips page and release notes. The workflow comes from the work realtors describe in public comments, and from how those features behave on a Mac.
Where realtors lose time in a browser

The most useful public signal comes from Sifta. The company analyzed 7,439 public comments from r/realtors and r/RealEstate, collected in July 2026. Transaction paperwork and deadlines ranked second, with 319 of 1,767 theme mentions, or 18.1%. Chasing people for documents and updates ranked fifth, at 10.1%. These are Reddit comments, not a survey, so read them as a pattern.

Look at what did not make the list. Logins were not a listed theme, and too many tools ranked tenth, at 2.1%. That does not mean logins are fine for you. It means the loudest complaint is the paperwork itself. Set Chrome up so paperwork and follow up are fast, and keep portal access out of your way.
Check your Chrome version before you change anything

Chrome updates itself, so most Macs run a recent build. Older Macs are the exception. Chrome 151 and later need macOS 13 or later. Chrome 150 is the last release that supports macOS 12. Google's enterprise release table lists Chrome 152 with a targeted stable date of September 1, 2026, so the current build may be newer than that.

items: Click Chrome in the menu bar, then choose About Google Chrome.
Wait while Chrome checks for updates.
Click Relaunch when the prompt appears, then confirm the version number again.

blocks.title: Old Mac, old Chrome
blocks.text: If your Mac runs macOS 12, you cannot install Chrome 151 or later. Chrome 150 is the last release for that system, so plan an operating system update before the browser falls behind.
Tab groups: one group per deal

Tab groups are the biggest single help for a busy agent. Make one group per property, and name it with the street address. Give it a color that shows the stage. Use one color for active listings and another for deals under contract. Put the MLS page, the seller disclosure, the title order and the lender thread inside.

items: Right-click a tab, then choose Add tab to new group.
Click the colored circle on the group to name it or change its color.
Drag tabs into the group, or drag them out to move them.

blocks.text: The common mistake is naming groups with a first name only. A few months later, nobody knows which Smith is which. Use the address and the stage, and add the MLS number if you use one. The group name is the only label you get, so make it do the work.
Pinned tabs for the portals you open every morning

Pinned tabs are for the pages you open every day. Pin your CRM, your email and your MLS search. Leave deal pages out of the pinned row. Deal pages change daily, and they belong in a group. A pinned row that holds only daily tools is faster to scan at the start of the day.

Pins do not log you in. If a portal asks for your password every morning, that is a separate problem. It may come from your browser settings or from the portal itself. Keep brokerage work in its own Chrome profile. Use the profile icon at the top right of the window to switch. That keeps work logins and personal logins apart.
Find any open tab with @tabs

Once you have several deal groups open, the tab strip gets crowded. Type @tabs in the address bar, then a space, then a few words. Chrome searches your open tabs and lists the matches. You skip the scroll and jump straight to the page.

items: @tabs inspection finds the inspection report you opened this morning.
@tabs lender finds the mortgage thread without a search through your email.
@tabs and the street name finds every page about one property.

blocks.text: Clear titles make the search easier. Name files before you open them, so the search has something useful to match. A page titled Final walkthrough notes is easier to find than one called Document (2).
Bookmark a deal before you close the window

Command+D bookmarks the current page. For a whole deal, choose More > Bookmarks > Bookmark All Tabs. Chrome bookmarks every open tab in the window. Use it at the end of a busy day, when the open tabs are the working file for one property and you want them back tomorrow.

blocks.title: Before you close the window
blocks.text: Bookmark All Tabs saves the pages, not the text you typed into them. Finish or save any half filled form before you close the window.
Mute, reopen and recover without losing your place

Auto-playing listing videos can start sound from a tab you forgot about. Chrome has a Mute site option. Use it, and the sound stops without closing the page. If you close the wrong tab, press ⌘⇧T to bring back the last one. Press it again to go back further.
Clear browsing data without losing your logins

Clearing browsing data helps when a portal misbehaves or a shared Mac holds old sessions. The shortcut is ⌘⇧⌫. Pick the time range and the data types before you confirm. Cookies and site data are the items that usually sign you out, so expect to log back in. Our guide on [clearing browsing data in Chrome](/how-to/clear-browsing-data-in-chrome) walks through the window.
Too many tools, and the AI tools agents never learn

Inman and Lofty ran a survey fielded from September 16 to October 2, 2026, with 460 responses. Lofty sells AI tools, so weigh the results with that in mind. In the survey, 45% of brokerage leaders said agents signed up for an AI tool and never learned to use it. Only 15% of agents said the same about themselves.

That gap is the warning. A tool that lives in a browser tab is easy to open once and forget. Pick the one that saves the most time, use it for a week, then decide. The same survey found 62% of agents pay for a general purpose AI assistant, and 14% pay for a real estate specific one.
Where AI fits in your Chrome workflow

NAR's 2026 REALTORS Technology Survey found 23% of REALTORS use AI tools daily. It found 55% say AI has had a positive effect on their business. Among AI users, 75% use it to write listing descriptions, 56% use it for social media posts, and 52% use it to draft emails and follow-ups.

Those three jobs fit a browser setup well. Keep listing copy in a tab beside the MLS, so you can check facts against the record. Keep the follow-up draft in your email tab, so you send it from the window where you wrote it. Drafting and sending are separate steps. Read every draft before it leaves your screen.
Signing links and the paperwork chase

NAR's 2025 survey found 79% of REALTORS use eSignature, so signing links are a daily Chrome task. When a signing link opens in a tab, drop it into the deal group. Once the envelope is complete, move the tab out or close it. A finished tab left open is one more thing to scan next week.

Chasing documents ranked fifth in the Sifta comments. A saved snippet helps here. Lazur keeps snippets, a personal dictionary and clipboard slots, so the request you send every week stays one hold away.

items: Open the deal group and find the item still missing.
Search your email tab for the document name, and check when it last went out.
Draft the request with the missing item named in the first line.
Hold fn and dictate the phone version, if you call instead.

blocks.text: Where Lazur fits in Chrome

Lazur is a voice assistant for the Mac that lives in the notch. Hold ⌥ ⌘ to ask about anything on screen, and Lazur answers out loud. Ask where something is, and Lazur draws a circle and a label around it. Ask how to do something, and Lazur guides you one click at a time, waiting for each click.

Lazur does not click buttons or operate Chrome for you. You keep the mouse. The Lazur for Chrome extension handles research jobs. Those run in Lazur's own Chrome tabs and come back with a summary and a report. Your own tabs stay yours.

Lazur listens and looks at the screen only while you hold the shortcut. Audio and the screenshot go to AI providers so they can answer, and they are not stored. Content is never used to train AI models. A screen with a client's bank details is still a client's bank details. Check your brokerage's data rules before you hold the shortcut on that page.
A listing week in Chrome, step by step

Say you list a condo on Monday, and it goes under contract later that week. On Monday, make one tab group named with the address, colored for active listings. Put the MLS page, the listing copy and the photo order inside. Pin your CRM and email, and leave the deal group where it is.

When the offer is accepted, recolor the group to show the deal is under contract. Add the inspection, lender and title tabs. If a buyer's agent asks for the HOA packet, type @tabs, a space, then HOA. Chrome lists the match. If a tab closes by accident, press ⌘⇧T.

Ask Lazur for help with the listing copy. Hold ⌥ ⌘, ask it to read the draft aloud, and ask what a buyer would still need to know. Lazur answers out loud. You make the edits. At the end of the week, use More > Bookmarks > Bookmark All Tabs to save the working set, then close the window clean.
Mistakes that slow realtors down in Chrome

items: Naming tab groups with a first name only. Use the address and the stage.
Pinning every portal, so the pinned row becomes a second tab strip.
Mixing personal and brokerage browsing in one profile.
Clearing all browsing data to fix one login. Cookies may sign you out of every site.
Letting Chrome fall behind on an old macOS. Check the version when a portal starts to act up.
Trying several AI tools in one week. Pick one and learn it first.

blocks.text: Most of these come from rushing. The fix is a slower setup once, then faster days after that.

What to set up this week

items: Update Chrome through Chrome > About Google Chrome, then confirm your macOS version is 13 or later.
Make one tab group for each active deal, and name it with the street address.
Pin your CRM, your email and your MLS search, and nothing else.
Try @tabs once on a crowded window, so the habit sticks.
Set up a separate Chrome profile for brokerage work.

faq.question: Is there a special Chrome for realtors on Mac?
faq.answer: No. Chrome for realtors on Mac is the standard Google Chrome app. The difference comes from setup: tab groups, pinned tabs, a separate profile for brokerage work and a few shortcuts. Nothing special needs to be installed for real estate work.

faq.question: Which macOS version does Chrome need?
faq.answer: Chrome 151 and later need macOS 13 or later. Chrome 150 is the last release that supports macOS 12. Google's enterprise release table lists Chrome 152 with a targeted stable date of September 1, 2026. Check your own version under Chrome > About Google Chrome.

faq.question: How do I find an open tab quickly in Chrome?
faq.answer: Type @tabs in the address bar, then a space and a few words. Chrome searches your open tabs and lists the matches. Clear page titles make the search faster, so name documents before you open them.

faq.question: Does Lazur click buttons in Chrome for me?
faq.answer: No. Lazur does not click buttons, edit files or operate other apps. When you ask how to do something, it guides you one click at a time and waits for each click. When you ask where something is, it circles the spot on screen.

faq.question: Does Lazur send client data to AI providers?
faq.answer: Lazur listens and looks at the screen only while you hold the shortcut. Audio and the screenshot go to AI providers to answer, and they are not stored. Content is never used to train AI models. Check your brokerage's data rules before you share client information this way.

faq.question: Is Lazur available for Windows?
faq.answer: Not yet. Windows is planned, not available. Lazur runs on macOS, on both Apple silicon and Intel Macs.

faq.question: Where can I see Lazur pricing?
faq.answer: Check the [pricing page](/pricing) for current plans. Lazur offers a trial that needs no credit card, and it starts when you first open the app.
